Agents should treat them as history; the live leaves inflation-ended and burn-2019 carry the history that still matters. (2) Price prediction and investment advice. (6) stellar-core internals (bucket list, parallel apply design). current-protocol and protocol-history cover what users see; core-ops covers operators. (7) Per-project leaves beyond Blend, Soroswap, Aquarius, and Comet/Phoenix. These four have concentrated mined demand. All other projects fall under project-lookup, project-builders, and project-funding-history. (8) Pi Network's own tokenomics. pi-network covers only its relation to Stellar. (9) Stellar Open Institute and other dormant programs.

DEMAND-SOURCE LIMITS. The Stack Exchange API (observed 2026-11-14, 1,456 questions) skews toward 2017-2019. Its top-voted questions are about inflation, nodes, and SCP; its recent questions are mostly retail support (wrong memo, phishing, Pi, wrong chain). Discord is not indexed on the web: the search returned only the SCF handbook's Discord navigation page. eval/discovery/mined-lumenloop-queries.json was generated by agents from committed eval questions (sourcePolicy says no raw user traffic), so its concentration on 8 topics reflects eval design rather than user demand. Weights lean on GitHub issue comment counts (stellar-cli, rs-soroban-sdk, js-stellar-sdk, stellar-rpc, freighter, stellar-protocol, stellar-docs since 2024-06) and on persona searches.

RAVEN SPOT-CHECK METHOD. 52 of 156 leaves checked, all 27 weight-3 leaves first. Each checked leaf got one Raven search. Executes grouped 4 to 7 leaves per script, with at least one targeted operation call per leaf. A verdict records what Raven returned; it does not judge whether the content is true. Results: 38 yes, 10 partial, 4 no.
